All four tool invocations were issued against the harness and every one returned "Tool not found." None of the web-access or MCP tools are registered in this child runtime.

## Results

| Test | Result | Evidence |
|------|--------|----------|
| (a) `web_search{query:"Vea kleros optimistic bridge", provider:"brave"}` | **FAIL** | No result returned; harness error `Tool web_search not found` |
| (b) `fetch_content{url:"https://example.com"}` | **FAIL** | No `<h1>` obtained; harness error `Tool fetch_content not found` |
| (c) `mcp{search:"navigate"}` | **FAIL** | No navigate tool name obtained; harness error `Tool mcp not found` |
| (d) `mcp{tool:"browser_browser_navigate", args:{url:"https://example.com"}}` | **FAIL** | No page `<title>` obtained; harness error `Tool mcp not found` |

### Verbatim errors

- (a) `web_search`:
  ```
  Tool web_search not found
  ```
- (b) `fetch_content`:
  ```
  Tool fetch_content not found
  ```
- (c) `mcp{search:"navigate"}`:
  ```
  Tool mcp not found
  ```
- (d) `mcp{tool:"browser_browser_navigate", ...}`:
  ```
  Tool mcp not found
  ```

### Ground-truth conclusion

Every tool was actually invoked (not merely described). The harness returned `Tool <name> not found` for all four, which is authoritative evidence that `web_search`, `fetch_content`, and `mcp` are **not registered in this child runtime's tool menu**. The provider extensions (pi-web-access, pi-mcp-adapter) were not activated in this subagent's runtime, so the requested tool names were pruned from the effective allowlist before the first model turn.

Note: `mcp{tool:...}` for (d) could not exercise a different code path because the `mcp` proxy tool itself is absent; the navigate tool name `browser_browser_navigate` was supplied from inherited context rather than obtained from a successful (c) call.
